name: Hip House
about: Hip house put rap verses over house beats, and for a few years around 1988 to 1991 it was the sound of the charts on both sides of the Atlantic. Chicago's Fast Eddie and Tyree Cooper, who claimed to have invented it with Turn Up the Bass, and New York's Jungle Brothers, whose I'll House You was produced by Todd Terry, set the template: a 120-beat-per-minute drum-machine groove, a piano or sampled stab, and a rapper working the crowd. British producers behind the Beatmasters, D Mob and the Cookie Crew made it pop, and European acts such as Technotronic and Snap! sold millions. It faded fast, but its DNA runs through 2 Unlimited, Azealia Banks and the house records of recent R&B.

albums.title: It Takes Two
albums.why: The title track's Lyn Collins break and shouted hook became the template for rap over a dance groove; the album is a singles collection with a classic in it.

albums.title: Straight Out the Jungle
albums.why: Todd Terry's I'll House You sits on the Native Tongues' debut beside Afrocentric jazz-rap, and the whole record still sounds relaxed and new.

albums.title: Jack to the Sound
albums.why: Chicago's first hip house album, rough and loud, with Fast Eddie rapping over jack tracks; the crude original of the style.

albums.title: Turn Up the Bass
albums.why: Tyree Cooper's claim to have invented hip house rests on the title track, and the album around it is DJ International house with a rapper on top.

albums.title: Twin Hype
albums.why: The New Jersey twins' Profile debut, with Do It to the Crowd, is the East Coast hip house moment caught quickly and cheaply.

albums.title: In Flightt
albums.why: Planet E and Let's Get Jazzy made KC Flightt New York's jazzier hip house voice; the album is uneven but has more ideas than most.

albums.title: Pump Up the Jam: The Album
albums.why: Jo Bogaert's Belgian studio project, with Ya Kid K rapping, sold millions on the title track and Get Up!; cheap, catchy and genre-defining.

albums.title: Anywayawanna
albums.why: Rhythm King's house team with the Cookie Crew, Merlin and Betty Boo; Rok da House and Hey DJ are British hip house at its most chart-ready.

albums.title: A Little Bit of This, A Little Bit of That
albums.why: Dancin' Danny D's album carries We Call It Acieed and It Is Time to Get Funky; a document of London's house-pop crossover, slight but lively.

albums.title: Born This Way!
albums.why: The London duo's debut mixes hip house with Daddy-O and Gang Starr productions; Got to Keep On is the house classic.

albums.title: All Hail the Queen
albums.why: Come Into My House is one of the great hip house singles, and Latifah's debut surrounds it with reggae, jazz-rap and Ladies First.

albums.title: Done by the Forces of Nature
albums.why: Less house than the debut but a richer record, with What U Waitin' 4? keeping the dancefloor and the rest reaching for jazz and Africa.

albums.title: Get Busy
albums.why: The Chicago producer's Jive album, with Get Busy and Pump That Body, is the most polished pure hip house record of the era.

albums.title: Doug Lazy Gettin' Crazy
albums.why: Let It Roll and Let the Rhythm Pump made Doug Lazy a club name; the album is solid Atlantic-funded hip house with little else.

albums.title: World Power
albums.why: The Power and Ooops Up made the Frankfurt studio act global stars; Turbo B's raps and Penny Ford's vocals carry a stronger album than expected.

albums.title: Dreamland
albums.why: Ride on Time and Everybody Everybody are Italo house more than hip house, but the Bologna trio's album defined the pop end of the moment.

albums.title: Down to Earth
albums.why: The British Native Tongues member's debut moves between hip house and jazz-rap; Monie in the Middle and It's a Shame are the keepers.

albums.title: World Clique
albums.why: Groove Is in the Heart, with Q-Tip and Bootsy Collins, is the hip house pop record, and the album is New York club culture at its most joyful.

albums.title: Gonna Make You Sweat
albums.why: Freedom Williams' raps and Martha Wash's vocals on the title track made Clivillés and Cole's album the biggest hip house record in America.

albums.title: Broke with Expensive Taste
albums.why: 212 revived hip house for a new decade, and the long-delayed album around it is restless, eclectic and better than its chaos suggests.

note: Hip house was a singles form with a short life, so this shelf includes the pop and Euro records it crossed into and stops at twenty.
